description: Simulate `make` WITHOUT RUNNING ANYTHING: which targets would be rebuilt, in what order, and WHY, naming the file to blame. Answers the two questions no other tool answers: "why is it rebuilding this when I changed nothing?" and "why is it NOT rebuilding it?". With `project` it reads the Makefile and the REAL mtimes from disk; `touch` asks "what if I changed this file?" without changing it. The reasons use the same vocabulary as the Linux kernel's `make V=2`.

files.description: List of project paths, if no folder is given

forceAll.description: Like `make -B`: rebuild everything without looking at dates

project.description: Project folder: its Makefile and its files' real mtimes are read

targets.description: What to build. Empty = the Makefile's default target

text.description: The Makefile pasted, if there is no folder

touch.description: Files to treat as just-modified, WITHOUT actually touching them (like `make -W`)

name: make_simulate
